key_insight: PI-GINOT learns geometry-conditioned hyperelastic responses for DogBone specimens without finite-element training data by combining a geometry encoder, cross-attention decoding, and physics-based losses.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster virtual testing and geometry optimization for nonlinear solid mechanics when repeated finite-element simulations would be too expensive.
method: Encodes each specimen’s boundary point cloud into geometry features.
Uses a cross-attention decoder to predict displacement at arbitrary interior points.

Enforces boundary conditions exactly and trains with physics losses from equilibrium, traction-free/symmetry, stability, and internal-force consistency; stresses are obtained by automatic differentiation with a compressible Neo-Hookean plane-stress model.
evidence_signal: Validated on eight unseen geometries with displacement errors of 2.1%–7.1%, peak von Mises stress errors of 0.9%–13.3%, and section-force errors below 10.3% using Abaqus only for post-training validation.
watch_item: Local stress components remain less accurate, especially in narrow specimens where steep gradients near the gauge-to-fillet transition are difficult to resolve.
paper_title: PI-GINOT: Data-free geometry-informed neural operator learning for finite-strain hyperelasticity on parametric DogBone specimens
